items.stem: What does an `ICacheFeed<X>` let the engine read?

options.text: The destination's current state, so the engine can diff against it

items.explanation: The cache feed re-reads the destination's current entities so the engine can compute the diff and garbage-collect.

misconceptions.a: Reading the source is the IFeed's job; the cache feed reads the destination.

items.stem: Why is the cache feed usually implemented on the same class as the sink?

options.text: A class can implement only one interface, so they must merge
Both talk to the destination, so one class avoids duplicating that access code — and a class can implement multiple interfaces
The engine requires them to share a base class
It makes the feed read the source faster

items.explanation: The sink already knows how to reach the destination; implementing ICacheFeed<T> on the same class reuses that — and one class can implement several interfaces.

misconceptions.a: A class can implement many interfaces; that's exactly what makes the combination possible.

items.stem: The cache feed's LoadEntities() reads from which side?
items.explanation: The cache feed reports the destination's current entities; the source-side snapshot comes from the IFeed.

misconceptions.a: That's the IFeed. The cache feed is the destination-side reader.

items.stem: Take an existing `CourseSink : ISink<Course>` and make one class that is both the sink and the cache feed. Show the class declaration and a LoadEntities() that returns the destination's current courses.
rubric: Single class implements both ISink<Course> and ICacheFeed<Course>
Keeps the [Sink] attribute and the injected service
LoadEntities() returns IEntityCollection<Course> from the destination service (e.g. service.GetAll())

items.stem: Besides the source feed, why does the engine also need a cache feed?
rubric: The source feed only provides the source snapshot
The engine needs the destination's current state to diff against (and to garbage-collect) — that's what the cache feed supplies
items.sampleAnswer: The source feed gives the engine the new source snapshot, but to know what actually changed on the destination — and to garbage-collect records whose source disappeared — the engine must also read the destination's current state. The cache feed provides that.
